newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett to cut 250 jobs, revamp medical products unit.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett to cut 250 jobs, revamp medical products unit.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. said Tuesday it will cut 250 jobs as it consolidates product lines and abolishes divisions in a restructuring of its Medical Products Group.
The company said it expects to incur restructuring costs in the first and second quarters of 1997, but those costs "will not be materially significant," it said.
The company will consolidate its heart defibrillator and electrocardiograph product lines in McMinnville, Ore., into its Resuscitation Division in Andover, Mass.
Of the 152 employees affected, 100 will be offered new jobs in the Resuscitation Division. The transition will take 90 to 120 days, HP said.
HP's Healthcare Information Management Division in Andover will be disbanded, and most of its products and services will be transferred to other Medical Products Group divisions.
HP's CareVue clinical-information systems will be merged into the company's Patient Monitoring Division.
The company's stock fell 25 cents to $45.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
